analysis.title: US midterm elections: The blue wave came to fruition
key_insights: Natixis says the 'blue wave' is taking shape, with Democrats expected to take control of both the House and the Senate, though several states (notably Alaska) had not yet released results.
Natixis does not expect the elections to change tariffs, immigration or the Iran war, because foreign trade and foreign policy remain under executive control.
Natixis expects Democrats to put renewed emphasis on healthcare and environmental policies, which could pressure the fiscal outlook.
The initial market reaction was a repricing of risk: lower equities and USD and declining Treasury yields, on the belief that a Democratic takeover would limit deficit expansion under Trump's agenda.
Yesterday's session was volatile, with optimism over a possible US-Iran agreement fading after reports of progress were denied.
The STOXX 600 fell 0.6%, its worst session since October 22. Healthcare was the only sector to rise, and consumer discretionary lagged on Zalando and CTS Eventim.
US semiconductors rebounded: the SOX rose 3.2% at the close of the European session after a cumulative loss of more than 11% over the previous three sessions. The VIX stayed above 20.

AMD reported Q3-26 revenue of $13.4bn (+45% YoY) against $13.1bn consensus, and EPS of $2.09 against $1.95 expected. Q4 revenue guidance of $17bn compares with a $16.3bn forecast. Shares rose 7% after hours.
AMD Data Center was 64% of revenue, up from 47% a year ago, which lowers its exposure to the weakening PC market relative to Intel.
The RBA raised interest rates, and AUD/USD fell 0.41% to 0.70.
Credit: iTraxx Main widened 0.3 bps and Xover 2 bps, while CDX tightened 0.7 bps. European airline CDS tightened on Lufthansa's results and lower oil prices. Alstom CDS widened 9 bps.
Equinix issued €2.5bn across four tranches, and Stellantis issued €500m 2-year at MS+97 bps with an 18 bps new issue premium and 3.8x oversubscription.

Intesa Sanpaolo (ISPIM) Q3-26: revenue of €6.9bn (+4% YoY) missed on a €27mn trading loss, while net income rose 12% YoY to €2.6bn. FY2026 profit guidance was raised to 'well above €10bn' despite an expected €1bn tax hit from the Italian Budget Law.
Raiffeisen (RBIAV) Q3-26: operating results were good and CoR beat expectations, but the bottom line missed on another Russia-related one-off. Guidance was raised for NII and loan growth.
France plans to raise the Livret A savings cap from €22,950 to between €25,000 and €30,000, with the increase planned for February.

market_movers.rationale: Q3-26 revenue and EPS beat consensus and Q4 revenue guidance of $17bn is above the $16.3bn forecast. Data Center is 64% of revenue.

sector_views.rationale: Healthcare was the only European sector to post a positive performance yesterday. Natixis expects Democrats to emphasize healthcare policy.

earnings_insights: AMD Q3-26 (reported, after hours 11/4): revenue $13.4bn (+45% YoY) vs consensus $13.1bn. EPS $2.09 vs $1.95 expected. Q4 revenue guidance $17bn vs $16.3bn forecast.
Intesa Sanpaolo Q3-26 (reported): revenue €6.9bn (+4% YoY) missed, net income €2.6bn (+12% YoY), FY2026 profit guidance raised to 'well above €10bn'.
Raiffeisen (RBIAV) Q3-26 (reported): revenues and expenses in line, CoR beat, bottom line missed on a Russia-related one-off. NII and loan growth guidance raised.
Lufthansa, Bayer and Philips reported results that tightened their CDS spreads. Figures are not given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Remains below 5%. Yields declined on the initial election reaction.
The hike pushed AUD/USD down 0.41% to 0.70.

risk_factors: A Democratic Congress could push healthcare and environmental policy that pressures the fiscal outlook.
US-Iran negotiation headlines are volatile and reports of progress have been denied.
Several states, including Alaska, had not released results, so the midterm outcome was not final at the time of writing.
The weakening PC market is a headwind for AMD relative to its Data Center growth.
vol_and_positioning: The VIX remained above 20. VIX futures stood at 19.6 (-0.5 on the day).
The SOX rebounded 3.2% after losing more than 11% cumulatively over the previous three sessions.
geopolitical: The US midterm elections point to Democratic control of the House and Senate, while Natixis expects trade, immigration and Iran war policy to stay under executive control.
Optimism over a potential US-Iran agreement faded after reports of progress in discussions were denied.
The Middle East conflict continues to weigh on markets, and Brent is down 10.0% over five days.
